L15: cite3†Global Affairs L16: # Snowflake and OpenAI partner to bring frontier intelligence to enterprise data
L17: 
L18: Loading…
L19: 
L20: Share
L21: 
L22: Key takeaways:
L23: 
L24:   * New $200 million agreement brings OpenAI frontier intelligence directly into Snowflake.
L25: 
L26:   * Enterprise customers can use OpenAI within Snowflake to build AI agents and generate insights directly from their data.
L27: 
L28:   * Under the partnership, OpenAI is one of the key model capabilities in Snowflake.
L29: OpenAI and Snowflake have entered a multi-year, $200 million partnership that brings OpenAI frontier intelligence directly into Snowflake, including cite4†Snowflake Cortex AI⁠(opens in a new window)†www.snowflake.com and cite5†Snowflake Intelligence⁠(opens in a new window)†www.snowflake.com .
L30: Snowflake is a data and AI platform that 12,600+ companies use to build, use, and share data, applications, and AI. With Snowflake, organizations can harness the power of their data and activate AI with an AI Data Cloud that’s intuitive and easy to use, seamlessly connected for collaboration, and built with the security and governance that enterprises trust as their foundation.
L31: Under the partnership, Snowflake customers can use OpenAI models like GPT‑5.2 with tools like Snowflake Cortex AI to build custom applications and agents grounded in their enterprise data. They can also use OpenAI within Snowflake Intelligence to ask questions in natural-language and put insights at every employee’s fingertips—automatically taking the steps needed to retrieve and analyze business data, without requiring users to write any code themselves.
L32: “By bringing OpenAI models to enterprise data, Snowflake enables organizations to build and deploy AI on top of their most valuable asset using the secure, governed platform they already trust,” said Sridhar Ramaswamy, CEO, Snowflake. “Customers can now harness all their enterprise knowledge in Snowflake together with the world-class intelligence of OpenAI models, enabling them to build AI agents that are powerful, responsible, and trustworthy.
L33: Together, we’re setting a new standard for AI innovation, helping businesses transform with confidence, while maintaining strong security and compliance standards.”
L34: “Snowflake is a trusted platform that sits at the center of how enterprises manage and activate their most critical data,” said Fidji Simo, CEO of Applications at OpenAI. “This partnership brings our advanced models directly into that environment, making it easier to deploy AI agents and apps, so businesses can close the gap between what AI is capable of and the value they can create today.”
L35: Additionally, with Snowflake Cortex AI Functions, teams can call OpenAI models directly from SQL to analyze any kind of data. Whether it’s rows and columns, text, images, or audio, AI becomes a natural extension of the language they already know and trust.
L36: ## Accelerating enterprise AI adoption
L37: 
L38: With OpenAI and Snowflake, customers can now apply powerful reasoning, analysis, and multimodal intelligence directly to their trusted data, enabling enterprises to deploy AI faster and at greater scale worldwide.
L39: Snowflake supports organizations across a wide range of industries—including financial services, healthcare, retail, media, manufacturing, and the public sector—helping teams in every vertical use data to run their businesses more effectively. The possibilities unlocked by this partnership are already resonating with enterprises:
L40: “As we scale our visual AI offering on Canva, both OpenAI and Snowflake have played key roles in how we rapidly empower our users with new creative tools,” said Helen Crossley, Head of Data Science, Canva. “As our platform continues to scale, Snowflake has been foundational to how we manage and activate data, and we’re excited to explore how leveraging OpenAI models in Snowflake Cortex AI can help us extend that foundation.
L41: The ability to bridge advanced AI models with our enterprise data allows us to move quickly and test new ideas, without compromising on security or performance.”
L42: “Speed and precision in decision-making are critical for us as WHOOP continues to scale,” said Matt Luizzi, Senior Director of Business Analytics, WHOOP. “Rolling out Snowflake Intelligence to our employees and developing Cortex Agents has provided a secure and governed way for WHOOP to analyze data and make decisions.
L43: With OpenAI’s models available directly within Snowflake Cortex AI, we can further enhance those agents with advanced reasoning and analysis, all while maintaining strong security and governance. This partnership will help us continue to make AI a practical, everyday tool for the business.”
L44: Moving forward, Snowflake and OpenAI teams will work closely together to bring new features that leverage OpenAI Apps SDK, AgentKit, and APIs that support shared enterprise workflows. As part of this effort, Snowflake will continue using ChatGPT Enterprise to help employees make decisions faster, streamline workflows, and collaborate more effectively.
L45: Snowflake extends OpenAI’s work with the world’s largest and most established enterprises, including cite6†Accenture⁠ , cite7†Walmart⁠(opens in a new window)†corporate.walmart.com , cite8†PayPal⁠(opens in a new window)†newsroom.paypal-corp.com , cite9†Intuit,⁠ cite10†Target⁠ , cite11†Thermo Fisher⁠(opens in a new window)†corporate.thermofisher.com , cite12†BNY⁠ , cite13†Morgan Stanley⁠ , cite14†BBVA⁠ , and many more.
L46: More than 1 million business customers around the world are directly using OpenAI—the cite15†fastest-growing business platform⁠ in history.

L172: ## GLM-OCR
L173: 
L174: cite82†中文阅读 L175: 
L176: 👋 Join our cite86†WeChat and cite87†Discord†discord.gg community
L177: 📖 Check out the GLM-OCR cite88†technical report†arxiv.org L178: 📍 Use GLM-OCR's cite89†API†docs.z.ai L179: ### Model Introduction
L180: GLM-OCR is a multimodal OCR model for complex document understanding, built on the GLM-V encoder–decoder architecture. It introduces Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) loss and stable full-task reinforcement learning to improve training efficiency, recognition accuracy, and generalization. The model integrates the CogViT visual encoder pre-trained on large-scale image–text data, a lightweight cross-modal connector with efficient token downsampling, and a GLM-0.5B language decoder.
L181: Combined with a two-stage pipeline of layout analysis and parallel recognition based on PP-DocLayout-V3, GLM-OCR delivers robust and high-quality OCR performance across diverse document layouts.
L182: Key Features
L183: 
L184:   * State-of-the-Art Performance: Achieves a score of 94.62 on OmniDocBench V1.5, ranking #1 overall, and delivers state-of-the-art results across major document understanding benchmarks, including formula recognition, table recognition, and information extraction.
L185: 
L186:   * Optimized for Real-World Scenarios: Designed and optimized for practical business use cases, maintaining robust performance on complex tables, code-heavy documents, seals, and other challenging real-world layouts.
L187:   * Efficient Inference: With only 0.9B parameters, GLM-OCR supports deployment via vLLM, SGLang, and Ollama, significantly reducing inference latency and compute cost, making it ideal for high-concurrency services and edge deployments.
L188: 
L189:   * Easy to Use: Fully open-sourced and equipped with a comprehensive cite62†SDK and inference toolchain, offering simple installation, one-line invocation, and smooth integration into existing production pipelines.
L190: ### News & Updates
L191: 
L192:   * [2026.3.12] GLM-OCR SDK now supports agent-friendly Skill mode — just `pip install glmocr` + set API key, ready to use via CLI or Python with no GPU or YAML config needed. See: cite90†GLM-OCR Skill L193:   * [2026.3.12] GLM-OCR Technical Report is now available. See: cite88†GLM-OCR Technical Report†arxiv.org L194:   * [2026.2.12] Fine-tuning tutorial based on LLaMA-Factory is now available. See: cite91†GLM-OCR Fine-tuning Guide L195: ### Download Model

L202: ## GLM-OCR SDK
L203: 
L204: We provide an SDK for using GLM-OCR more efficiently and conveniently.
L205: ### Install SDK
L206: 
L207: Choose the lightest installation that matches your scenario:
L208: 
L209:     # Cloud / MaaS + local images / PDFs (fastest install)
L210:     pip install glmocr
L211: 
L212:     # Self-hosted pipeline (layout detection)
L213:     pip install "glmocr[selfhosted]"
L214: 
L215:     # Flask service support
L216:     pip install "glmocr[server]"
L217: Install from source for development:
L218: 
L219:     # Install from source
L220:     git clone https://github.com/zai-org/glm-ocr.git
L221:     cd glm-ocr
L222:     uv venv --python 3.12 --seed && source .venv/bin/activate
L223:     uv pip install -e .
L224: ### Model Deployment
L225: 
L226: Two ways to use GLM-OCR:
L227: #### Option 1: Zhipu MaaS API (Recommended for Quick Start)
L228: 
L229: Use the hosted cloud API – no GPU needed. The cloud service runs the complete GLM-OCR pipeline internally, so the SDK simply forwards your request and returns the result.
L230: 
L231:   1. Get an API key from cite94†https://open.bigmodel.cn†open.bigmodel.cn L232:   2. Configure `config.yaml`:
L233: 
L234:     pipeline:
L235:       maas:
L236:         enabled: true # Enable MaaS mode
L237:         api_key: your-api-key # Required
L238: That's it! When `maas.enabled=true`, the SDK acts as a thin wrapper that:
L239: 
L240:   * Forwards your documents to the Zhipu cloud API
L241:   * Returns the results directly (Markdown + JSON layout details)
L242:   * No local processing, no GPU required
L243: Input note (MaaS): the upstream API accepts `file` as a URL or a `data:<mime>;base64,...` data URI. If you have raw base64 without the `data:` prefix, wrap it as a data URI (recommended). The SDK will auto-wrap local file paths / bytes / raw base64 into a data URI when calling MaaS.
L244: 
L245: API documentation: cite95†https://docs.bigmodel.cn/cn/guide/models/vlm/glm-ocr†docs.bigmodel.cn L246: #### Option 2: Self-host with vLLM / SGLang
L247: 
L248: Deploy the GLM-OCR model locally for full control. The SDK provides the complete pipeline: layout detection, parallel region OCR, and result formatting.
L249: 
L250: Install the self-hosted extra first:
L251: 
L252:     pip install "glmocr[selfhosted]"

L285: #### Option 3: Ollama/MLX

L289:   * cite96†Apple Silicon with mlx-vlm - Optimized for Apple Silicon Macs

L291: #### Option 4: SDK Server + Client (GPU-less Client)
L292: 
L293: Deploy the SDK Server on a GPU machine, then use any machine as a client — no GPU needed on the client side. The client connects via the MaaS-compatible protocol, pointing `api_url` at your self-hosted server.
L294: 
L295:     # Client config.yaml
L296:     pipeline:
L297:       maas:
L298:         enabled: true
L299:         api_url: http://<SERVER_IP>:5002/glmocr/parse
L300:         api_key: any-string    # self-hosted server does not validate keys
L301:         verify_ssl: false
L302: See the full guide: cite98†Self-hosted SDK Server + Client L303: #### Update Configuration
L304: 
L305: After launching the service, configure `config.yaml`:
L306: 
L307:     pipeline:
L308:       maas:
L309:         enabled: false # Disable MaaS mode (default)
L310:       ocr_api:
L311:         api_host: localhost # or your vLLM/SGLang server address
L312:         api_port: 8080

L314: ### SDK Usage Guide
L315: #### CLI
L316: 
L317:     # Parse a single image
L318:     glmocr parse examples/source/code.png
L319: 
L320:     # Parse a directory
L321:     glmocr parse examples/source/
L322: 
L323:     # Set output directory
L324:     glmocr parse examples/source/code.png --output ./results/
L325: 
L326:     # Use a custom config
L327:     glmocr parse examples/source/code.png --config my_config.yaml
L328: 
L329:     # Enable debug logging with profiling
L330:     glmocr parse examples/source/code.png --log-level DEBUG
L331:     # Run layout detection on CPU (keep GPU free for OCR model)
L332:     glmocr parse examples/source/code.png --layout-device cpu
L333: 
L334:     # Run layout detection on a specific GPU
L335:     glmocr parse examples/source/code.png --layout-device cuda:1
L336: 
L337:     # Override any config value via --set (dotted path, repeatable)
L338:     glmocr parse examples/source/code.png --set pipeline.ocr_api.api_port 8080
L339:     glmocr parse examples/source/ --set pipeline.layout.use_polygon true --set logging.level DEBUG
L340: #### Python API
L341: 
L342:     from glmocr import GlmOcr, parse
L343: 
L344:     # Simple function
L345:     result = parse("image.png")
L346:     result = parse(["img1.png", "img2.jpg"])
L347:     result = parse("https://example.com/image.png")
L348:     result.save(output_dir="./results")
L349: 
L350:     # Note: a list is treated as pages of a single document.
L351: 
L352:     # Class-based API
L353:     with GlmOcr() as parser:
L354:         result = parser.parse("image.png")
L355:         print(result.json_result)
L356:         result.save()
L357:     # Place layout model on CPU (useful when GPU is reserved for OCR)
L358:     with GlmOcr(layout_device="cpu") as parser:
L359:         result = parser.parse("image.png")
L360: 
L361:     # Place layout model on a specific GPU
L362:     with GlmOcr(layout_device="cuda:1") as parser:
L363:         result = parser.parse("image.png")
L364: #### Flask Service
L365: 
L366: Install the optional server dependency first:
L367: 
L368:     pip install "glmocr[server]"
L369: 
L370:     # Start service
L371:     python -m glmocr.server
L372: 
L373:     # With debug logging
L374:     python -m glmocr.server --log-level DEBUG
L375: 
L376:     # Call API
L377:     curl -X POST http://localhost:5002/glmocr/parse \
L378:       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
L379:       -d '{"images": ["./example/source/code.png"]}'
L380: 
L381: Semantics:
L382:   * `images` can be a string or a list.
L383:   * A list is treated as pages of a single document.
L384:   * For multiple independent documents, call the endpoint multiple times (one document per request).
L385: ### Modular Architecture
L386: 
L387: GLM-OCR uses composable modules for easy customization:
L388: 
L389: Component  | Description
L390: --- | ---
L391: `PageLoader`  | Preprocessing and image encoding
L392: `OCRClient`  | Calls the GLM-OCR model service
L393: `PPDocLayoutDetector`  | PP-DocLayout layout detection
L394: `ResultFormatter`  | Post-processing, outputs JSON/Markdown
L395: You can extend the behavior by creating custom pipelines:
L396: 
L397:     from glmocr.dataloader import PageLoader
L398:     from glmocr.ocr_client import OCRClient
L399:     from glmocr.postprocess import ResultFormatter
L400: 
L401: 
L402:     class MyPipeline:
L403:       def __init__(self, config):
L404:         self.page_loader = PageLoader(config)
L405:         self.ocr_client = OCRClient(config)
L406:         self.formatter = ResultFormatter(config)
L407: 
L408:       def process(self, request_data):
L409:         # Implement your own processing logic
L410:         pass
